question: Close the four layer-0 pool-integrity zero regions (first at layer=0 slot=18 kind=0 owner_expert=252) that appeared when the skip0 fix put layer 0 into the pool: are they a fill defect -- a routed token's layer-0 FFN silently computed as zero -- or the checkpoint's own content?

evidence.reading: File-side census over the full row stride, 31488 gate/up/down expert rows: 10 rows have a zero leading run (4592, 6560, 7216, 11152, 13120 B ...) and are 17.8-47.0% non-zero overall -- layer 0 gate/up experts 25/195/205/252, layer 1 gate/up expert 214. All 31478 other rows have leading_zero_run == 0. Stride 335872 B/expert == the nb02 the engine prints, and the tensor view is (256, 512, 656) uint8, so the read window is the engine's own.

The two instruments name the same row from opposite sides: the MMID assert fires on `ffn_moe_gate-0 ne02=143 ... first_id=18` (slot id) while the teardown scan prints `first zero region: layer=0 slot=18 kind=0 owner_expert=252`. The log's own slot table confirms the mapping independently: `CGC-POST: il=0 st[43]=43 st[238]=17 st[252]=18 st[25]=25 ...`. Expert 25 is the second census row on that line, and 4 = {25,252} x {gate,up} -- consistent with `layer=0 zero=4 of 142 resident slots`. Experts 195/205 never appear with a slot, i.e. were never demanded in this run.

The scan's inference was 'at teardown nothing is in flight, so a zero region is a fill bug by construction', which rests on the unstated premise that a correctly filled region is never all-zero in its first 4 KiB. `slot_owner` is written BEFORE fill_pool_direct (:827 then :831), so owner-set does not imply filled -- the test is structurally right; only its width was wrong.

After the two-tier probe: `pool integrity: owner-set slots=5935 zero-regions=0 zero-prefix-only=4` and `zero_row=1 (first_id=214) | zero_full=0 (first_id=-1, total=0)`. Gate vs v4: M1 9/9, M2 9/9, M3 9/9, full_fnv1a64 9/9, comparable=true. Launch-env fingerprint unchanged (e68a5dc537d626622a9af6c9c7ddf665).

`verify-strict: refused=1  zero_mapped_selected=0`. The one mechanism that DOES silently drop an expert's contribution is the reserved ZERO slot, and it is counted unconditionally and reported as 0: no token was ever served a zeroed region in place of its expert.

reasoning: The instrument could not have answered the question it was asked. Its probe is 4096 bytes; the file rows in question carry a 7216-byte zero prefix (expert 252, layer 0, gate), so the probe window lies entirely inside legitimately zero data. The adjudicator shared that width and therefore always agreed. Widening the confirmation to the whole stride resolves it in the direction that requires no action: the region matches the file, 138 of layer 0's 142 resident slots hold non-zero bytes so layer-0 fills demonstrably land, and the count 4 equals exactly two resident zero-prefix experts times gate+up. The complementary drop-detector reads 0. So the four regions are the checkpoint's own zero prefixes and the appearance of four instead of the old two is a visibility change, not a quality change: with skip0 ON, layer 0's slots were never owner-set, so the scan never looked at them. What does still change between the arms is the numerics, and that was already established separately by the +142 owner-set delta (5793 -> 5935 = exactly one layer) and the M1 4/9-versus-v3 gate result -- the zero-region count is not, and never was, the discriminator for 'layer 0 entered the pool'; it is a content readout whose value moves with the resident set. Two side effects worth keeping: the reported `zero-regions` now means what its own comment always claimed, and CGC_MMID_ASSERT_FATAL is usable at last -- it used to abort on these rows, i.e. on every healthy run of this model.
conclusion: Not a defect. The four layer-0 zero regions are the GGUF's own zero prefixes (experts 25 and 252, gate+up), the probe width was the bug, and no token had a layer-0 expert silently zeroed. Case closed; nothing on this path blocks the 250/25 work.
action: Landed as a two-tier probe in both instruments: ggml-metal-ops.cpp now reports `zero_row` (probe-wide) alongside `zero_full` (whole-row-confirmed) and gates CGC_MMID_ASSERT_FATAL on the confirmed one; llama-expert-cache.cpp reports `zero-regions` (whole stride) alongside `zero-prefix-only`. mmid_zero_row_triage.py now reads the whole stride, names PROBE-TOO-NARROW, exits 3 to mean 'fix the probe', and adjudicates pool-integrity alarms too, resolving slot->expert from the pool-integrity line itself. gguf_dead_expert_census.py added as the no-log file-side census. CONVENTIONS A13 added. Deliberately NOT done: re-baselining the gate (the change is print-only: fingerprint unchanged, and M1/M2/M3/fnv1a64 9/9 against the unchanged v4 reference).

question: prefill 250 tok/s has been measured repeatedly (254.74 / 264.78 / peak 276.59) and missed repeatedly by the same command (122.68, and a 2.25x four-launch spread on 09-15). Is it a spec reachable under a stated launch precondition, or a draw? The candidate mechanism was launch-time memory state: the prefill250 shape (13.66 GiB model + 8 GiB pool + a 6144-wide ubatch compute buffer) is over-subscribed on 16 GB, and run_server.sh:427-434 already documents that +2 GiB of pool pushes the 6144 compute buffer out of the GPU.

evidence.reading: Five independent processes, one identical command each (the env resolved by run_server.sh CGC_DUMP_ENV=1 through llama_bench_matrix.py, so the command is never retyped): 286.67 +-12.24 / 173.54 +-19.41 / 155.62 +-10.70 / 166.06 +-1.52 / 166.63 +-4.81 t/s. Spread 84.2%. Only run 1 cleared 250, and run 1 had the LEAST free memory (3.90 GiB vs 7.3-7.7) and the shortest wall (45 s vs 61-71 s). Within-run stddev is 1.52-19.41 (<=11.2%), so the spread is between processes, not measurement noise.

Instrument corrected to record File-backed pages (the actual page cache) and Anonymous pages, plus a --warm-runs option that pre-reads the whole 13.66 GB model before the launch. Six runs, cache forced high on runs 2/4/6: cache 4.51 / 9.61 / 2.98 / 9.89 / 2.32 / 9.96 GiB (4.3x range), free 3.74 / 0.07 / 7.81 / 0.06 / 7.26 / 0.06 GiB. Throughput 179.09 / 184.09 / 184.06 / 173.76 / 155.33 / 175.23 -- 0/6 cleared 250, spread 18.5%, and rho = +0.09 (cache), -0.14 (usable%), +0.14 (anon). Forcing the candidate variable 4.3x moved nothing.

evidence.reading: Batch 1 run 1: free 3.90 GiB, swap 3485 MiB -> 286.67 t/s. Batch 2 run 1: free 3.74 GiB, cache 4.51 GiB, swap 4452 MiB -> 179.09 t/s. Nearly identical launch state, 60% apart. This single pair refutes 'the draw is a machine memory state' more cleanly than either correlation, and it also means the one 286.67 sample is NOT reproducible from the state that was recorded alongside it.

Confirms what the 25 target depends on. cgc_pool_max_tokens() defaults to 8 and the clamp `cparams.n_batch = pmax` is still applied to every config without CGC_PREFILL_STREAM; the M2 slab path is the only thing that lifts it, and only for prefill ('Decode / MTP verify still run n_tokens<=pmax through the pool path'). The decoupling that would remove the clamp, CGC_POOL_SPLIT (M1 work item 1), exists but its own document says 'Status: implemented, measured, and rejected', llama.cpp:424 logs it as 'EXPERIMENTAL, KNOWN-BROKEN (degenerate routing + SIGSEGV)', and llama-context.cpp:268-278 records that the clamp is deliberately NOT lifted even with an owned pool. Blocker B's signature is two experts owning one slot (`CGC-POST: il=1 st[0]=1 st[1]=1`) -> NaN at il=2.

reasoning: The hypothesis was falsifiable in two ways and failed both. First direction: if throughput tracks launch memory, the faster runs must have more of it available -- instead rho was -0.70, and the fastest run had the least. That sign inversion is what exposed the instrument error (free is a sum of two opposite-signed effects), so the experiment was re-run with the page cache recorded explicitly and then FORCED, which is the only way to separate 'this variable causes it' from 'state accumulates with run order'. Second direction: cache went up 4.3x and throughput did not move at all (rho +0.09). With both candidates dead, the remaining explanation has to live in the engine's own state rather than the machine's counters -- and the decisive pair (near-equal launch state, 60% apart) says the recorded state does not even determine the outcome. Meanwhile the code read settles the other half of the question: the decode target's blocker is not missing work but a measured rejection, so 'nothing is blocking 250/25' was wrong in both halves.
conclusion: prefill 250 is a draw at the prefill250 shape: 1/11 independent runs cleared it, and the operating point is the 155-184 t/s band (18.5%). Machine memory state does not explain the spread -- neither free memory nor the page cache, the latter despite being forced 4.3x. The correction of a plausible fix (gate the launch on free memory / warm the cache) is worth more than the negative result itself: it was cheap to refute and would otherwise have been shipped as a precondition that does nothing. Separately, the decode half is blocked by M1 being 'implemented, measured, and rejected', not by work not done.

ruled_out.why_false: rho(usable%, t/s) = -0.70 in batch 1 and -0.14 in batch 2: the sign is wrong, and the run with the least free memory (3.90 GiB) was the only one to clear 250. `Pages free` is the sum of two opposite-signed effects (large page cache vs large anonymous footprint) and is not a measure of either.

question: §8 第 1 項：把 `CGC-DECPROF` 的列印閘門打開之後，prefill 的慢是「某一層變慢」還是「全層等比變慢」？前者指向實作，後者指向時脈／功耗。

evidence.reading: :2080 的閘門改為 `((dp_step % 8) == 0 || dp_step == 1 || dp_ntok > 1)`；:1864/:2011/:2132 新增 `dp_ntok`（讀 `as_topk[i]->ne[1]`）；:2084 行尾追加 `ntok=%lld`。

第一次開啟就輸出 90 行，形狀為 `step=1..4 ntok=2048`（四次 prefill，各 ~6.7-7.4 s、41 segs / 40 layers）然後 `step=8..48 ntok=1`（decode）。prefill 的三段拆分是 wait 85-98% / cb 1-13% / submit 0-2%；decode 是 wait 43-76% / cb 21-53% / submit 3-5%。該次 pp=285.58 t/s。

reasoning: 三個獨立讀數指向同一個答案。第一，逐層比值在七層上幾乎是常數（CV 6.5%），而且那個常數（2.32×）等於吞吐損失（2.33×）——一致到 0.5% 以內。若成本集中在某一層，比值會出現一個離群峰，而不是一條平線。第二，慢跑內部 40 層的 wait 分布（IQR/中位數 0.094）顯示每一層幾乎一模一樣慢。第三，唯一偏離的那一層是 L0 且比值 <1 側（1.11 而非 ~2.3），而 L0 在快跑裡也是最低的一層（112 ms 對 155 ms 平台）——所以那是 `submit_ahead` 管線的填充暫態（第 i 層只等得到前 i 層累積的 GPU 工作量），與快慢狀態無關，不能當成「某層沒變慢」的反例。把三點合起來：整張 prefill 圖以同一倍率變慢，倍率等於吞吐損失 ⇒ 依 §3 與 §6 的判準，這指向**時脈／功耗上限**，而不是實作熱點。這也把 §3/§3.1 的「GPU 忙著」推進到「GPU 以固定倍率變慢」。

DBUF2 交換只在 `il == 1 && n_tokens == 1 && cgc_dbuf2_on()` 觸發（預設關）；zero slot 是 `slots_l - 1`（最後一個），不是 slot 0。

reasoning: 先做可證的排除。`CGC_DBUF2` 的交換會讓 `slot_table` 與 `slot_owner` 描述不同世界，這是症狀最直接的解釋——但它預設關閉，且只在 verify-decode 的單 token 步觸發，而文件的重現指令沒有開它。所以它被排除，不是嫌疑犯。接著得到一個具體且可檢驗的線索：身分映射把所有 slot 的 `last_use` 設成同一個值 0，而 `pick_slot` 的 LRU 在平手時以掃描序決定，於是 slot 0（expert 0）系統性地成為第一個犧牲者。這正好對上症狀裡「st[0] 掉了而 st[1..7] 都還在」的不對稱——在 legacy（pool 就是張量本身的儲存）路徑下同樣的 `last_use=0` 存在，但那一組 slot 同時也是 loader 預讀過的位元組，所以被逐出後重建的成本與語意不同；owned pool 把這兩件事拆開了。最後一個發現是 blocker B 目前**不能**照文件引用來修：`CGC-POST` 與 `CGC-SLOT` 共用同一份 `st` 快照，而 `remap` 是用那份快照逐格寫的，所以 `st[1]=1` 與 `remap[1]=2` 在同一次列印裡不可能同時成立。引文至少有一處不是該行原文，因此「兩個 expert 共用一 slot」的機制尚未被正確地記錄下來。
